Roasted Pumpkin Cream Soup

Creme de abóbora assada
SoupsEasy ●○○⏱ 45 minServes 4
Your rating:
Prep10 min
Cook35 min
Total45 min
DifficultyEasy ●○○
Serves4
Calories~190 kcal
Protein5 g
Fat11 g
Carbs15 g

Estimated nutrition per serving, calculated from the ingredients.

Orange, creamy soup with a hint of sweetness — roasting the pumpkin makes all the difference.

🧺 Ingredients

For 4 people
  • 800 g pumpkin, cut into cubes
  • 1 onion, cut into quarters
  • 2 cloves garlic
  • 700 ml vegetable stock or hot water
  • 2 tbsp olive oil
  • 100 ml heavy cream (optional)
  • salt, pepper and a pinch of nutmeg

👩‍🍳 Method

  1. Preheat the oven to 200°C.💡 Why it matters: A hot oven from minute one makes cakes and roasts rise and brown evenly. In a cold oven, the cooking time changes and so does the result.
  2. Put the pumpkin, onion and garlic on a baking tray. Drizzle with olive oil, salt and pepper.
  3. Roast for 25 minutes, until soft and golden at the edges.
  4. Move everything to a pot, add the stock and let it simmer for 5 minutes.
  5. Blend with an immersion blender until you have a smooth cream.
  6. Add the cream and nutmeg, taste and adjust the salt. Serve hot, with a drizzle of olive oil on top.💡 Why it matters: Tasting at the end is what separates 'almost good' from 'really good': salt, acidity and heat can be fixed in seconds — but only if you taste.

📸 The process, in photos — and why each phase matters

💡 Lili's tip
Roasting the pumpkin before cooking it is the trick: it gets a sweet, toasted flavor that plain boiled soup doesn't have.
🍽️ What to serve with it
Garlic toast · Toasted pumpkin seeds · Crunchy croutons · A little grated cheese on top

Oven-Roasted Chicken Legs with Carrot Rice

Pernas de frango assadas no forno com arroz de cenoura
MeatEasy ●○○⏱ 60 minServes 4
Your rating:
Prep15 min
Cook45 min
Total60 min
DifficultyEasy ●○○
Serves4
Calories~610 kcal
Protein33 g
Fat27 g
Carbs62 g

Estimated nutrition per serving, calculated from the ingredients.

Crispy skin, juicy chicken, and fluffy orange rice on the side.

🧺 Ingredients

For 4 people
  • 4 chicken legs
  • 2 tbsp olive oil
  • 1 tsp paprika
  • 1 tsp garlic powder
  • 0,5 lemon (the juice)
  • 300 g rice
  • 2 grated carrots
  • 1 chopped onion
  • 2 cloves minced garlic
  • 600 ml hot water
  • 1 leaf bay leaf
  • salt and pepper

👩‍🍳 Method

  1. Season the chicken with olive oil, paprika, garlic powder, lemon juice, salt and pepper. Let it pick up flavor for 10 minutes.
  2. Oven at 200°C: roast for 40 to 45 minutes, turning halfway. It's ready when the skin is golden and crispy.💡 Why it matters: Browning creates brand-new flavor — it's the reaction that gives color and depth. Wet food or a cold pan steams instead of browning, so dry things well and don't crowd the pan.
  3. In a pot, sauté the onion and garlic in a drizzle of olive oil for 3 minutes. Add the grated carrot and stir for 2 more minutes.
  4. Add the rice, stir for 1 minute, then add the hot water, bay leaf and salt.
  5. Cover and cook over low heat for 12 minutes. Turn off the heat and let it rest for 5 minutes.💡 Why it matters: Resting isn't wasted time: juices redistribute and doughs relax. Cutting or unmolding too early loses liquid, air and texture.
  6. Fluff the rice with a fork and serve with the chicken on top and a slice of lemon.

📸 The process, in photos — and why each phase matters

💡 Lili's tip
If you have time, season the chicken in the morning and keep it in the fridge. By dinner the flavor is much better.
🍽️ What to serve with it
Simple green salad · Roasted vegetables · Yogurt sauce with garlic and lemon · Mild piri-piri, for those who like it

Couscous with Roasted Vegetables & Dried Fruit

Couscous de legumes assados e frutos secos
Rice & GrainsEasy ●○○⏱ 25 minServes 4

🧺 Ingredients

For 4 people
  • 250 g couscous
  • 250 ml hot stock
  • 1 zucchini, cut into cubes
  • 1 red bell pepper, cut into cubes
  • 1 carrot, cut into small cubes
  • 1 red onion
  • 50 g dried fruit (raisins and chopped apricot)
  • 40 g almonds or chopped walnuts
  • 1 tsp cumin
  • 0,5 lemon (the juice)
  • olive oil, salt, pepper and cilantro or mint
Your rating:
Prep10 min
Cook15 min
Total25 min
DifficultyEasy ●○○
Serves4
Calories~410 kcal
Protein10 g
Fat14 g
Carbs55 g

Estimated nutrition per serving, calculated from the ingredients.

Light, colorful and quick: fluffy couscous with sweet vegetables and a touch of dried fruit.

👩‍🍳 Method

  1. Sauté or roast the vegetables in olive oil for 8 to 10 minutes, until soft and golden. Season with salt, pepper and cumin.
  2. Boil the stock and pour it over the couscous in a bowl. Cover and wait 5 minutes.💡 Why it matters: Boiling too hard breaks delicate ingredients and can curdle sauces with cream or egg. A gentle simmer is almost always enough — and safer.
  3. Fluff the couscous with a fork and add a drizzle of olive oil.
  4. Mix in the vegetables, dried fruit and almonds.
  5. Add the lemon juice and chopped herbs. Taste and adjust the salt.💡 Why it matters: Tasting at the end is what separates 'almost good' from 'really good': salt, acidity and heat can be fixed in seconds — but only if you taste.
  6. Serve warm — it's great freshly made and the next day too.

📸 The process, in photos — and why each phase matters

🍽️ What to serve with it

Grilled chicken on the sideBaked salmonTomato saladYogurt sauce with mint
Lili's tipDon't cook couscous like pasta. You just hydrate it with hot stock, covered — otherwise it turns to mush.

Portuguese Kale Soup

Caldo verde
SoupsEasy ●○○⏱ 35 minServes 4
Your rating:
Prep10 min
Cook25 min
Total35 min
DifficultyEasy ●○○
Serves4
Calories~175 kcal
Protein5 g
Fat8 g
Carbs22 g

Estimated nutrition per serving, calculated from the ingredients.

The Portuguese classic: a potato cream with very finely cut kale and a drizzle of olive oil.

🧺 Ingredients

For 4 people
  • 500 g potatoes, cut into cubes
  • 1 onion
  • 2 cloves garlic
  • 200 g very finely sliced Galician kale (or kale)
  • 1200 ml water
  • 4 slices chorizo (optional)
  • olive oil and salt

👩‍🍳 Method

  1. Cook the potatoes, onion and garlic in salted water for 20 minutes.
  2. Blend everything until you have a smooth cream. If it's too thick, add a little more hot water.
  3. Put it back on the heat. When it boils, add the very finely cut kale.💡 Why it matters: Boiling too hard breaks delicate ingredients and can curdle sauces with cream or egg. A gentle simmer is almost always enough — and safer.
  4. Cook only 5 to 7 minutes — the kale should stay bright green and tender, not brown.💡 Why it matters: Browning creates brand-new flavor — it's the reaction that gives color and depth. Wet food or a cold pan steams instead of browning, so dry things well and don't crowd the pan.
  5. Add a good drizzle of olive oil and adjust the salt.💡 Why it matters: Tasting at the end is what separates 'almost good' from 'really good': salt, acidity and heat can be fixed in seconds — but only if you taste.
  6. Serve piping hot, with a slice of chorizo on top of each bowl.

📸 The process, in photos — and why each phase matters

💡 Lili's tip
Cut the kale as thin as you can. And don't overcook it: it loses its color and flavor.
🍽️ What to serve with it
Corn bread (broa) · Homemade bread for dipping in the soup · A drizzle of good olive oil on top

Hake Fillets with Russian Salad

Filetes de pescada com salada russa
FishMedium ●●○⏱ 35 minServes 4

🧺 Ingredients

For 4 people
  • 4 hake fillets
  • 100 g flour
  • 1 beaten egg
  • 100 g breadcrumbs
  • 3 potatoes, cut into cubes
  • 2 carrots, cut into cubes
  • 150 g peas
  • 3 tbsp mayonnaise
  • 0,5 lemon
  • olive oil, salt and pepper
Your rating:
Prep20 min
Cook15 min
Total35 min
DifficultyMedium ●●○
Serves4
Calories~440 kcal
Protein23 g
Fat19 g
Carbs35 g

Estimated nutrition per serving, calculated from the ingredients.

Breaded, golden fish with that creamy salad of potato, carrot and peas.

👩‍🍳 Method

  1. Cook the potato, carrot and peas in salted water. Drain and let cool.💡 Why it matters: Cooling before cutting or frosting stops cakes from falling apart and frosting from melting and sliding off. The structure sets outside the oven.
  2. Mix the vegetables with the mayonnaise, a few drops of lemon and pepper. Keep in the fridge.💡 Why it matters: Cold firms up creams and doughs and makes everything easier to cut and handle — and it's also a safety thing with cream and eggs.
  3. Season the fillets with salt, pepper and lemon. Coat each one in flour, then egg, then breadcrumbs.
  4. Heat olive oil in a skillet and fry for 3 to 4 minutes on each side, until golden. (In the oven: 200°C, 15 minutes.)
  5. Rest the fillets on paper towels for a minute, to drain the extra oil.💡 Why it matters: Resting isn't wasted time: juices redistribute and doughs relax. Cutting or unmolding too early loses liquid, air and texture.
  6. Serve with the nice and cold Russian salad and lemon slices.

📸 The process, in photos — and why each phase matters

🍽️ What to serve with it

Green saladFluffy white riceOven potatoes instead of fried
Lili's tipRussian salad made the day before tastes even better — the flavors come together in the fridge.

PastaEasy ●○○⏱ 25 minServes 4

Quick pasta with sautéed vegetables and crunchy toasted almond on top.

👩‍🍳 Method

  1. Cook the pasta in well-salted water, for the time on the package. Save a cup of the cooking water.💡 Why it matters: Cooking water holds starch and salt: it helps sauces bind, shine and cling to the food instead of staying watery on the plate.
  2. In a dry skillet, toast the almonds for 2 minutes until fragrant. Remove and set aside.
  3. In the same skillet, sauté the garlic and vegetables in olive oil for 6 to 7 minutes. The tomato goes in at the end.
  4. Add the drained pasta and a little of the cooking water. Stir well, 1 minute.💡 Why it matters: Cooking water holds starch and salt: it helps sauces bind, shine and cling to the food instead of staying watery on the plate.
  5. Turn off the heat. Add the basil and Parmesan.
  6. Serve with the toasted almonds on top — they're what gives the crunch.

Layers of pasta, meat with tomato and béchamel, with golden cheese on top.

👩‍🍳 Method

  1. Sauté the onion and garlic in olive oil. Add the meat and let it brown well, stirring to break it up.💡 Why it matters: Browning creates brand-new flavor — it's the reaction that gives color and depth. Wet food or a cold pan steams instead of browning, so dry things well and don't crowd the pan.
  2. Add the tomato, paste, oregano, salt and pepper. Cook over low heat for 15 minutes.💡 Why it matters: Low heat gives sauces time to thicken and flavors time to come together, without burning the bottom or curdling cream and eggs.
  3. If you make the béchamel at home: melt 50 g of butter, add 50 g of flour, then 500 ml of milk a little at a time, always stirring until it thickens. Season with salt and nutmeg.
  4. In a baking dish, build layers: a little béchamel, pasta sheets, meat, béchamel. Repeat 3 times.
  5. Finish with béchamel and the grated cheese over everything.
  6. Oven at 180°C for 30 minutes, until golden and bubbling. Let it rest for 10 minutes before cutting — it slices much better.💡 Why it matters: Resting isn't wasted time: juices redistribute and doughs relax. Cutting or unmolding too early loses liquid, air and texture.

  1. Preheat the oven to 200°C. Cut the vegetables into large pieces.💡 Why it matters: A hot oven from minute one makes cakes and roasts rise and brown evenly. In a cold oven, the cooking time changes and so does the result.
  2. Put them on a tray with olive oil, salt, pepper and thyme. Roast for 30 minutes, until soft and golden at the edges.
  3. Move everything to a pot, add the stock and let it boil for 5 minutes.💡 Why it matters: Boiling too hard breaks delicate ingredients and can curdle sauces with cream or egg. A gentle simmer is almost always enough — and safer.
  4. Blend until you have a smooth cream.
  5. Taste and adjust the seasonings.💡 Why it matters: Tasting at the end is what separates 'almost good' from 'really good': salt, acidity and heat can be fixed in seconds — but only if you taste.
  6. Serve hot, with a drizzle of olive oil or cream.

📸 The process, in photos — and why each phase matters

💡 Lili's tip
Compare it with Wednesday's Vegetable Cream: same vegetables, different technique. Roasting changes everything.

A grilled cheese toast (our tosta mista) · Toast · Garlic croutons

PastaMedium ●●○⏱ 25 minServes 4

The Roman classic: creamy pasta with egg and cheese, no cream — the trick is in the technique.

👩‍🍳 Method

  1. Cook the spaghetti in well-salted water. Save a cup of the cooking water — you'll need it.💡 Why it matters: Cooking water holds starch and salt: it helps sauces bind, shine and cling to the food instead of staying watery on the plate.
  2. Fry the guanciale in a large skillet, with no oil, until golden and crispy. Turn off the heat.💡 Why it matters: Browning creates brand-new flavor — it's the reaction that gives color and depth. Wet food or a cold pan steams instead of browning, so dry things well and don't crowd the pan.
  3. In a bowl, beat the yolks, the egg, the cheese and plenty of pepper. It becomes a thick paste.
  4. Drain the pasta and add it to the skillet, off the heat.💡 Why it matters: Draining well removes extra water or oil — the stuff that softens crusts, thins sauces and makes salads soggy.
  5. Add the egg mixture and a little of the cooking water. Stir fast — the heat of the pasta makes a creamy sauce, without cooking the egg.💡 Why it matters: Cooking water holds starch and salt: it helps sauces bind, shine and cling to the food instead of staying watery on the plate.
  6. Serve right away, with more cheese and pepper on top.

📸 The process, in photos — and why each phase matters

🍽️ What to serve with it

A simple green saladA glass of water with lemon, to cut the richnessBread to mop up the sauce
Lili's tipOff the heat, always. If the skillet is boiling, the egg turns into an omelet — and carbonara should be creamy.

Tiramisu

Tiramisù
Prep · 25 min|Cook · 0 min|Serves · 6|~500 kcal
Your rating:

Layers of ladyfingers soaked in coffee and a light mascarpone cream. No oven.

🧺 Ingredients

For 6 people
  • 250 g mascarpone cheese
  • 200 ml heavy cream, very cold, for whipping
  • 3 eggs (yolks and whites separated)
  • 80 g sugar
  • 200 g ladyfinger cookies
  • 250 ml strong coffee, already cold
  • cocoa powder, for dusting

👩‍🍳 Method

  1. Beat the yolks with the sugar until you have a pale, fluffy cream.
  2. Add the mascarpone and stir until combined, without overbeating.
  3. Whip the cream until firm and fold it into the cream. Whip the egg whites to stiff peaks and fold them in too, gently.💡 Why it matters: Folding gently keeps the air in beaten egg whites and whipped cream — that air is the lightness. Beating hard throws it away.
  4. Dip each ladyfinger in the coffee — quickly, just get it wet, or it falls apart.
  5. Build layers in a dish: ladyfingers, cream, ladyfingers, cream.
  6. Keep in the fridge for at least 4 hours (overnight is ideal). Dust with cocoa before serving.💡 Why it matters: Cold firms up creams and doughs and makes everything easier to cut and handle — and it's also a safety thing with cream and eggs.

Crispy puff pastry and a cinnamon egg custard. Warm, fresh out of the oven, it's something else.

🧺 Ingredients

For 6 people
  • 1 roll puff pastry
  • 250 ml milk
  • 150 g sugar
  • 3 tbsp flour
  • 4 egg yolks
  • 1 stick cinnamon and 1 lemon peel
  • ground cinnamon and powdered sugar, for serving

👩‍🍳 Method

  1. Bring the milk to a simmer with the cinnamon and lemon until almost boiling. Remove from the heat.💡 Why it matters: Boiling too hard breaks delicate ingredients and can curdle sauces with cream or egg. A gentle simmer is almost always enough — and safer.
  2. Mix the sugar with the flour and add a little of the hot milk, stirring. Then add it all back to the milk and cook, always stirring, until it thickens like a cream.
  3. Remove from the heat, let it cool for 5 minutes and add the yolks one at a time, stirring fast.💡 Why it matters: Cooling before cutting or frosting stops cakes from falling apart and frosting from melting and sliding off. The structure sets outside the oven.
  4. Roll out the puff pastry, roll it up like a log, cut slices and line muffin tins, spreading the pastry with wet thumbs.
  5. Fill the tins up to 3/4 with the custard.
  6. A very hot oven, 250°C, for 12 to 15 minutes, until the custard gets those toasted little spots. Serve warm, with cinnamon.

Mozambique's soul dish: cassava leaves in a peanut and coconut sauce.

👩‍🍳 Method

  1. If you use fresh leaves, pound or chop them very finely. Nowadays they're sold already pounded and frozen — it saves a lot of work.
  2. Boil the leaves in salted water for 20 minutes, to remove the bitterness. Drain.💡 Why it matters: Boiling too hard breaks delicate ingredients and can curdle sauces with cream or egg. A gentle simmer is almost always enough — and safer.
  3. Sauté the onion and garlic. Add the drained leaves.💡 Why it matters: Draining well removes extra water or oil — the stuff that softens crusts, thins sauces and makes salads soggy.
  4. Add the coconut milk and ground peanut, a little at a time, stirring so it doesn't stick.
  5. Cook over low heat for 20 to 25 minutes, stirring now and then, until the sauce is creamy and combined.💡 Why it matters: Low heat gives sauces time to thicken and flavors time to come together, without burning the bottom or curdling cream and eggs.
  6. If you make the shrimp version, add it in the last 5 minutes. Serve over fluffy white rice.

Chicken marinated and grilled with the piri-piri sauce that was born in Mozambique.

🧺 Ingredients

For 4 people
  • 1 whole chicken, butterflied (or 4 large legs)
  • 4 cloves crushed garlic
  • 2 piri-piri chilies (or to taste)
  • 1 lemon (the juice)
  • 3 tbsp olive oil or oil
  • 1 tsp paprika
  • salt, pepper and extra piri-piri sauce for serving

👩‍🍳 Method

  1. Make the marinade: mix the garlic, chopped piri-piri, lemon juice, olive oil, paprika, salt and pepper.💡 Why it matters: Marinating gives salt and spices time to get inside the food — the flavor ends up within, not just on the surface.
  2. Rub the chicken well on all sides. Let it marinate for at least 30 minutes — overnight is even better.💡 Why it matters: Marinating gives salt and spices time to get inside the food — the flavor ends up within, not just on the surface.
  3. Heat the grill well, or the oven to 200°C.
  4. Grill/roast the chicken for 30 to 35 minutes, turning and brushing with the marinade, until nicely golden with toasted skin at the edges.💡 Why it matters: Marinating gives salt and spices time to get inside the food — the flavor ends up within, not just on the surface.
  5. Let it rest for 10 minutes before cutting.💡 Why it matters: Resting isn't wasted time: juices redistribute and doughs relax. Cutting or unmolding too early loses liquid, air and texture.
  6. Serve with extra piri-piri sauce on the side — everyone adds the heat they can handle.

💡 Lili's tip
Heat is built up: start with little piri-piri in the marinade and serve extra sauce on the side. Taking heat away is what you can't do.

👩‍🍳 Method

  1. Season the chicken with garlic, salt, pepper, half the lime juice and a drizzle of oil. Let it sit for 20 minutes.💡 Why it matters: Resting isn't wasted time: juices redistribute and doughs relax. Cutting or unmolding too early loses liquid, air and texture.

  5. Put the grilled chicken on a platter and pour the hot sauce over it.

Cassava & Coconut Cake

Bolo de mandioca e coco
Prep · 15 min|Cook · 45 min|Serves · 6|~495 kcal
Your rating:

A moist, dense cake of grated cassava and coconut — a homemade snack, in Mozambique and in Brazil.

🧺 Ingredients

For 6 people
  • 500 g raw cassava, finely grated
  • 200 g sugar
  • 200 ml coconut milk
  • 100 g shredded coconut
  • 2 eggs
  • 50 g melted butter
  • 1 tsp baking powder
  • a pinch of salt

👩‍🍳 Method

  1. Preheat the oven to 180°C and grease a pan with butter and flour.💡 Why it matters: A hot oven from minute one makes cakes and roasts rise and brown evenly. In a cold oven, the cooking time changes and so does the result.
  2. Mix the grated cassava with the sugar, shredded coconut and salt.
  3. Add the eggs, melted butter and coconut milk. Stir well.
  4. Add the baking powder last and fold in gently.💡 Why it matters: Folding gently keeps the air in beaten egg whites and whipped cream — that air is the lightness. Beating hard throws it away.
  5. Pour into the pan and smooth the top.
  6. Bake for 40 to 45 minutes, until golden and a toothpick comes out almost clean. Let it cool before cutting — it slices much better warm/cold.💡 Why it matters: Cooling before cutting or frosting stops cakes from falling apart and frosting from melting and sliding off. The structure sets outside the oven.

Black beans cooked slowly with meats, served with everything it deserves.

🧺 Ingredients

For 6 people
  • 500 g black beans, soaked overnight
  • 300 g pork, cut into cubes (ribs or shoulder)
  • 200 g linguiça sausage, cut into slices
  • 150 g bacon, cut into cubes
  • 1 chopped onion
  • 3 cloves minced garlic
  • 2 leaves bay leaves
  • salt, pepper and oil

👩‍🍳 Method

  1. Cook the soaked beans in fresh water with the bay leaves, over low heat, for 40 minutes.💡 Why it matters: Low heat gives sauces time to thicken and flavors time to come together, without burning the bottom or curdling cream and eggs.
  2. Separately, brown the meats and sausage in a skillet. That browning is what gives feijoada its flavor.💡 Why it matters: Browning creates brand-new flavor — it's the reaction that gives color and depth. Wet food or a cold pan steams instead of browning, so dry things well and don't crowd the pan.
  3. Add the browned meats to the beans.💡 Why it matters: Browning creates brand-new flavor — it's the reaction that gives color and depth. Wet food or a cold pan steams instead of browning, so dry things well and don't crowd the pan.
  4. Sauté the onion, garlic and bacon and add that too, fat and all.
  5. Cook everything together for 40 to 50 more minutes, until the beans are soft and the broth is thick. Add hot water if it dries out.
  6. Adjust the salt at the end (the meats already bring salt). Serve very hot, with the sides alongside.💡 Why it matters: Tasting at the end is what separates 'almost good' from 'really good': salt, acidity and heat can be fixed in seconds — but only if you taste.

📸 The process, in photos — and why each phase matters

💡 Lili's tip
Feijoada is Saturday food, made calmly. Don't rush: low heat and time make the broth.

America's most famous comfort dish: pasta in a really creamy cheese sauce.

👩‍🍳 Method

  1. Cook the pasta in salted water, 1 minute less than the package says. Drain.💡 Why it matters: Draining well removes extra water or oil — the stuff that softens crusts, thins sauces and makes salads soggy.
  2. Melt the butter, add the flour, and cook for 1 minute, stirring — this is the roux, the base of the sauce.
  3. Add the milk a little at a time, stirring constantly, and cook until it thickens, about 5 minutes.

A gentle simmer is almost always enough — and safer.
  5. Add the pasta to the sauce and toss well.

🧺 Ingredients

For 4 people
  • 500 g ground beef (with some fat — 80/20 is ideal)
  • 4 burger buns
  • 4 slices cheddar or American cheese
  • lettuce, tomato, onion, and pickles
  • mayonnaise, ketchup, and mustard; salt and pepper; butter for the buns

👩‍🍳 Method

  1. Divide the beef into 4 balls and flatten them into patties a little wider than the buns (they shrink). Press a small dent in the center with your thumb.
  2. Season only with salt and pepper, on the outside, right when you're about to grill.
  3. Very hot grill or skillet: 3 to 4 minutes per side. Don't press the burger — all the juice runs out.
  4. In the last minute, put the cheese on top and cover, so it melts.
  5. Toast the cut buns in a skillet with a little butter.
  6. Build it: sauces on the bun, lettuce, tomato, the cheesy patty, onion, and pickles. Serve right away.

📸 The process, in photos — and why each phase matters

💡 Lili's tip
The dent in the middle isn't a quirk: it keeps the burger from puffing up into a ball instead of a disc.

A really creamy chowder, with sweet corn, potato, and a smoky touch from the bacon.

🧺 Ingredients

For 4 people
  • 400 g corn (fresh, frozen, or canned and drained)
  • 2 potatoes, cut into small cubes
  • 100 g bacon, cut into small cubes
  • 1 chopped onion
  • 2 cloves minced garlic
  • 700 ml chicken or vegetable broth
  • 200 ml heavy cream or whole milk
  • salt, pepper, thyme, and chives

👩‍🍳 Method

  1. Fry the bacon in a pot until crispy. Take it out and set it aside, leaving the fat in the pot.💡 Why it matters: Browning creates brand-new flavor — it's the reaction that gives color and depth. Wet food or a cold pan steams instead of browning, so dry things well and don't crowd the pan.
  2. Sauté the onion in that fat (or in olive oil) for 4 minutes. Add the garlic.
  3. Add the potato and the broth. Cook for 12 minutes, until the potato is tender.
  4. Add the corn and cook 5 more minutes.
  5. Blend one third of the soup (or mash some of the potato with a fork) — that's what makes it creamy without needing lots of cream.
  6. Add the cream, adjust the salt and pepper, and serve with the crispy bacon and chives on top.💡 Why it matters: Browning creates brand-new flavor — it's the reaction that gives color and depth. Wet food or a cold pan steams instead of browning, so dry things well and don't crowd the pan.

📸 The process, in photos — and why each phase matters

💡 Lili's tip
Blending only one third is the chowder trick: creamy, but still with chunks to chew.

Toast or saltine crackers, like in the US · A green salad · On its own, as a light winter meal

Ribs that fall right off the bone, with a sweet, smoky barbecue sauce. Low heat and time.

🧺 Ingredients

For 4 people
  • 1000 g pork ribs (spare ribs)
  • 2 tbsp brown sugar
  • 1 tbsp paprika (smoked, if you have it)
  • 1 tsp garlic powder
  • 1 tsp onion powder
  • 250 ml store-bought barbecue sauce (or homemade)
  • salt and pepper

👩‍🍳 Method

  1. Remove the thin membrane from the back of the ribs (pull it off with a paper towel — it comes off in one piece). It's what makes them tough.
  2. Mix the sugar, paprika, garlic and onion powders, salt, and pepper. Rub it well all over the meat.
  3. Wrap tightly in aluminum foil, meat side down.
  4. Low oven, 150°C, for 2½ hours. Low and slow — there are no shortcuts.💡 Why it matters: Low heat gives sauces time to thicken and flavors time to come together, without burning the bottom or curdling cream and eggs.
  5. Unwrap and brush generously with barbecue sauce.
  6. Back in the oven (or on the grill) at 200°C for 15 minutes, brushing once more, until the sauce is shiny and sticky. Rest 10 minutes and cut between the bones.💡 Why it matters: Resting isn't wasted time: juices redistribute and doughs relax. Cutting or unmolding too early loses liquid, air and texture.

📸 The process, in photos — and why each phase matters

💡 Lili's tip
The test is simple: the meat should give way and almost fall off the bone when you lift a rib with tongs. If it resists, it needs more time, not more heat.

Coleslaw · Boiled or grilled corn · French fries or roasted potatoes · Cornbread, for the full menu

American Apple Pie

Tarte de maçã americana
Prep · 30 min|Cook · 50 min|Serves · 6|~340 kcal
Your rating:

The pie from the movies: cinnamon apples inside a golden, flaky crust.

🧺 Ingredients

For 6 people
  • 2 sheets shortcrust or puff pastry (store-bought works fine)
  • 6 apples, peeled and thinly sliced
  • 120 g sugar
  • 1 tbsp flour
  • 1 tsp cinnamon
  • 1 tbsp lemon juice
  • 20 g butter, cut into small cubes
  • 1 beaten egg with a little milk, for brushing; a pinch of salt and nutmeg

👩‍🍳 Method

  1. Mix the apples with the sugar, flour, cinnamon, lemon, salt, and nutmeg. Let it sit 15 minutes — they release juice and soak up the flavor.💡 Why it matters: Resting isn't wasted time: juices redistribute and doughs relax. Cutting or unmolding too early loses liquid, air and texture.
  2. Line a pie dish with one sheet of pastry, leaving extra around the edges.
  3. Put the apples in, with the little butter cubes on top.
  4. Cover with the second sheet: either whole (with a few slits on top to let the steam out), or in crisscross strips, like in the classic photos.
  5. Trim and fold the edges, and brush with the beaten egg.💡 Why it matters: Folding gently keeps the air in beaten egg whites and whipped cream — that air is the lightness. Beating hard throws it away.
  6. Bake at 190°C for 45 to 50 minutes, until golden and the filling is bubbling. Let it cool for at least 1 hour before slicing, so the filling sets.💡 Why it matters: Cooling before cutting or frosting stops cakes from falling apart and frosting from melting and sliding off. The structure sets outside the oven.

Chocolate Cake with Creamy Frosting

Bolo de chocolate com cobertura cremosa
Prep · 20 min|Cook · 35 min|Serves · 8|~790 kcal
Your rating:

The fluffy chocolate cake with the creamy frosting from the techniques page. The birthday favorite.

🧺 Ingredients

For 8 people
  • 250 g flour
  • 75 g cocoa powder
  • 300 g sugar
  • 2 tsp baking powder
  • 3 eggs
  • 200 ml milk
  • 120 ml oil
  • 200 ml hot water
  • 200 g butter at room temperature (frosting)
  • 300 g powdered sugar (frosting)
  • 50 g cocoa (frosting) and 3 to 4 tbsp of milk

👩‍🍳 Method

  1. Oven at 180°C. Grease and flour a 22 cm round pan (or two 20 cm pans).💡 Why it matters: A hot oven from minute one makes cakes and roasts rise and brown evenly. In a cold oven, the cooking time changes and so does the result.
  2. Mix the dry ingredients: flour, cocoa, sugar, baking powder, and a pinch of salt.
  3. Add the eggs, milk, and oil and beat for 2 minutes. Pour in the hot water a little at a time — the batter will be runny, that's how it should be (it's what makes the cake moist).
  4. Bake for 30 to 35 minutes. The toothpick should come out with moist crumbs, not wet batter.
  5. Let it cool completely before frosting — frosting on a warm cake melts and slides off.💡 Why it matters: Cooling before cutting or frosting stops cakes from falling apart and frosting from melting and sliding off. The structure sets outside the oven.
  6. Creamy frosting: beat the butter for 2 minutes, add the sifted powdered sugar and cocoa and the milk, and beat until light and spreadable. Spread it between the layers and on top, with swirls of the spatula.💡 Why it matters: Sifting removes lumps and adds air to dry ingredients — lighter batters and sauces without little balls.

Brazilian Carrot Cake with Brigadeiro Frosting

Bolo de cenoura com cobertura de brigadeiro
Prep · 15 min|Cook · 40 min|Serves · 8|~780 kcal
Your rating:

Brazil's orange cake: carrots blended into the batter and a generous layer of soft brigadeiro on top.

🧺 Ingredients

For 8 people
  • 3 medium carrots, peeled
  • 4 eggs
  • 240 ml oil
  • 300 g sugar
  • 320 g flour
  • 1 tbsp baking powder
  • 1 can sweetened condensed milk (frosting)
  • 3 tbsp cocoa (frosting) and 1 tbsp of butter

👩‍🍳 Method

  1. Blend the carrots, eggs, oil, and sugar in the blender until you get a smooth orange cream.
  2. Pour it into a bowl, add the sifted flour, and stir. The baking powder goes in last — just fold it in.💡 Why it matters: Sifting removes lumps and adds air to dry ingredients — lighter batters and sauces without little balls.
  3. Greased 24 cm pan, oven at 180°C for 35 to 40 minutes.💡 Why it matters: A hot oven from minute one makes cakes and roasts rise and brown evenly. In a cold oven, the cooking time changes and so does the result.
  4. Frosting: put the condensed milk, cocoa, and butter in a pan over the heat, stirring constantly, until it thickens a little (soft brigadeiro stage, about 6 minutes).
  5. Pour the warm frosting over the warm cake — it should drip down the sides, just like that.

Chocolate Brownies

Brownie de chocolate
Prep · 15 min|Cook · 25 min|Serves · 8|~455 kcal
Your rating:

Dense, moist, and with that thin, shiny crust on top. It's not cake — it's a brownie.

🧺 Ingredients

For 8 people
  • 170 g butter
  • 200 g dark chocolate
  • 3 eggs
  • 200 g sugar
  • 90 g flour
  • 30 g cocoa
  • a pinch of salt; walnuts (if you like)

👩‍🍳 Method

  1. Melt the butter and chocolate together (microwave in short bursts, or a double boiler). Let it cool a little.💡 Why it matters: Boiling too hard breaks delicate ingredients and can curdle sauces with cream or egg. A gentle simmer is almost always enough — and safer.
  2. Beat the eggs and sugar for 2 minutes, until slightly thickened — that's what makes the shiny crust.
  3. Add the melted chocolate and stir.
  4. Fold in the flour, cocoa, and salt, just until the flour disappears.💡 Why it matters: Folding gently keeps the air in beaten egg whites and whipped cream — that air is the lightness. Beating hard throws it away.
  5. Lined 20 cm square pan, oven at 175°C for 22 to 25 minutes. The center should wobble slightly.💡 Why it matters: A hot oven from minute one makes cakes and roasts rise and brown evenly. In a cold oven, the cooking time changes and so does the result.
  6. Cool completely before cutting into squares — warm, it falls apart.💡 Why it matters: Cooling before cutting or frosting stops cakes from falling apart and frosting from melting and sliding off. The structure sets outside the oven.

No-Bake Berry Cheesecake

Cheesecake de frutos vermelhos
Prep · 25 min|Cook · 0 min|Serves · 8|~495 kcal

No oven: a crunchy cookie base, a light cream, and berries on top.

🧺 Ingredients

For 8 people
  • 200 g crushed digestive cookies
  • 80 g melted butter
  • 400 g cream cheese
  • 200 ml heavy cream, for whipping
  • 100 g powdered sugar and the juice of half a lemon
  • 200 g berries (fresh or frozen)

👩‍🍳 Method

  1. Mix the cookie crumbs with the butter and press firmly into the bottom of a 20 cm springform pan. Put it in the fridge.💡 Why it matters: Cold firms up creams and doughs and makes everything easier to cut and handle — and it's also a safety thing with cream and eggs.
  2. Beat the cream cheese with the sugar and lemon until smooth.
  3. Whip the cream until firm and fold it into the cheese, gently.💡 Why it matters: Folding gently keeps the air in beaten egg whites and whipped cream — that air is the lightness. Beating hard throws it away.
  4. Pour the cream over the base, smooth it out, and refrigerate for at least 4 hours (overnight is better).
  5. Before serving, cover with the berries (if frozen, thaw and drain them).💡 Why it matters: Draining well removes extra water or oil — the stuff that softens crusts, thins sauces and makes salads soggy.

Chicken Tikka Masala

Frango tikka masala
MeatMedium ●●○⏱ 50 minServes 4
Your rating:
Prep20 min

Total50 min
DifficultyMedium ●●○
Serves4
Calories~450 kcal
Protein48 g
Fat25 g
Carbs9 g

Estimated nutrition per serving, calculated from the ingredients.

The world's most famous Indian curry: chicken marinated in yogurt, in a creamy tomato and spice sauce.

🧺 Ingredients

For 4 people
  • 600 g chicken, cut into cubes
  • 150 g plain yogurt (marinade) and 2 cloves of garlic + grated ginger
  • 2 tsp garam masala
  • 400 g crushed tomatoes
  • 1 finely chopped onion
  • 150 ml heavy cream
  • oil, salt, paprika, and cilantro

👩‍🍳 Method

  1. Marinate the chicken in the yogurt with garlic, ginger, salt, and half the garam masala, for at least 30 minutes.💡 Why it matters: Marinating gives salt and spices time to get inside the food — the flavor ends up within, not just on the surface.
  2. Sear the chicken in a very hot skillet until it takes on color. Set aside (it doesn't need to be cooked through).💡 Why it matters: Browning creates brand-new flavor — it's the reaction that gives color and depth. Wet food or a cold pan steams instead of browning, so dry things well and don't crowd the pan.
  3. In the same skillet, sauté the onion until well golden. Add the tomato and the rest of the spices and cook for 10 minutes, until the sauce darkens and thickens.💡 Why it matters: Resting isn't wasted time: juices redistribute and doughs relax. Cutting or unmolding too early loses liquid, air and texture.
  4. Blend the sauce (optional, for a velvety texture) and return it to the skillet with the cream.
  5. Add the chicken and cook for 8 to 10 minutes in the sauce.
  6. Serve with cilantro on top.

📸 The process, in photos — and why each phase matters

💡 Lili's tip
A blended, well-reduced sauce is the difference between 'homemade curry' and 'restaurant curry'.
🍽️ What to serve with it
Basmati rice or jeera rice · Garlic naan · Raita (yogurt with cucumber) on the side
🔥 Calories
~450 kcal · protein 48 g

India's celebration rice: fragrant basmati layered with spiced chicken and fried onion.

👩‍🍳 Method

  1. Marinate the chicken in the yogurt with garlic, ginger, spices, and salt, for 30 minutes.💡 Why it matters: Marinating gives salt and spices time to get inside the food — the flavor ends up within, not just on the surface.
  2. Cook the rice in well-salted water with bay leaf and cardamom only to 70% — still firm in the middle. Drain.💡 Why it matters: Draining well removes extra water or oil — the stuff that softens crusts, thins sauces and makes salads soggy.
  3. Cook the marinated chicken in its pot for 15 minutes, until it forms a thick sauce.💡 Why it matters: Marinating gives salt and spices time to get inside the food — the flavor ends up within, not just on the surface.
  4. Layer it in the pot: rice, chicken, fried onion, herbs, a drizzle of the saffron milk. Repeat.
  5. Cover tightly (the lid wrapped in a cloth, the way it's done there) and cook on the lowest heat for 20 minutes, without opening.
  6. Rest for 10 minutes and fold it gently, from the bottom up, right at the table.💡 Why it matters: Resting isn't wasted time: juices redistribute and doughs relax. Cutting or unmolding too early loses liquid, air and texture.

Yogurt and cucumber raitaOnion and tomato saladNaan

  3. Taste: the cardamom should be felt only in the background, not take over.💡 Why it matters: Tasting at the end is what separates 'almost good' from 'really good': salt, acidity and heat can be fixed in seconds — but only if you taste.
  4. Serve in tall glasses, nice and cold.

📸 The process, in photos — and why each phase matters

After a spicy curry — it puts out the fire like nothing elseAs a snack, on its ownWith samosas, for a complete Indian snack

  1. Boil the cassava in salted water until very soft, about 25 minutes. Remove the fibrous core.💡 Why it matters: Boiling too hard breaks delicate ingredients and can curdle sauces with cream or egg. A gentle simmer is almost always enough — and safer.

A gluten-free crepe made with just tapioca starch, in a skillet, in three minutes.

👩‍🍳 Method

  1. Sift the starch straight into a cold nonstick skillet, spreading it in a thin, even layer.💡 Why it matters: Sifting removes lumps and adds air to dry ingredients — lighter batters and sauces without little balls.

Thin pastry half-moons with a shrimp cream filling — a party snack in Mozambique and Portugal.

👩‍🍳 Method

  1. Dough: boil the water with butter and salt, add the flour all at once, and stir until it forms a smooth ball.   1. Make a regular curry: sauté the onion, garlic, and ginger, add the curry powder and tomato, and cook for 10 minutes.
  2. Add the meat and potato and cook over low heat until tender and the sauce is thick, about 25 minutes.💡 Why it matters: Low heat gives sauces time to thicken and flavors time to come together, without burning the bottom or curdling cream and eggs.
  3. Cut the top off the loaf and pull out the soft inside carefully, without piercing the walls — the bread is the bowl.
  4. Fill it well with the hot curry and put the bread 'hat' back on top.
  5. Serve right away, with the scooped-out bread on the side for dipping. Eat with your hands.

📸 The process, in photos — and why each phase matters

🍽️ What to serve with it

Grated carrot salad with piri-piri (sambals)Yogurt, for the heatOn its own — it already comes with its 'bowl' and side
Lili's tipThe sauce has to be thick: a watery sauce soaks the bread and the bowl falls apart in your hand.

Chakalaka: spicy beans and vegetables. Pap: a firm white cornmeal porridge, a cousin of xima.

👩‍🍳 Method

  1. Chakalaka: sauté the onion, bell pepper and carrot in oil for 5 minutes. Add the curry powder and the tomato and cook for 10 minutes.
  2. Add the beans with a little of their liquid and cook for 10 more minutes. It should be thick and spicy. Adjust the salt.💡 Why it matters: Tasting at the end is what separates 'almost good' from 'really good': salt, acidity and heat can be fixed in seconds — but only if you taste.
  3. Pap: boil the water with salt. Pour the cornmeal in a thin stream, stirring constantly with a strong wooden spoon.💡 Why it matters: Boiling too hard breaks delicate ingredients and can curdle sauces with cream or egg. A gentle simmer is almost always enough — and safer.
  4. Cook the pap over low heat for 20 minutes, stirring hard now and then, until it is firm and pulls away from the pot.💡 Why it matters: Low heat gives sauces time to thicken and flavors time to come together, without burning the bottom or curdling cream and eggs.
  5. Serve the pap in small mounds with the chakalaka on top or on the side.

Grilled meat (braai!) — the classic pairingRoast chickenGreen salad

An apricot sponge cake soaked in a hot butter-and-cream sauce while still warm. Pure comfort.

👩‍🍳 Method

  1. Beat the eggs and sugar until fluffy. Add the apricot jam.
  2. Fold in the flour and baking soda, alternating with the milk mixed with vinegar.💡 Why it matters: Folding gently keeps the air in beaten egg whites and whipped cream — that air is the lightness. Beating hard throws it away.
  3. Greased baking dish, oven at 180°C for 30 to 35 minutes, until well golden.💡 Why it matters: A hot oven from minute one makes cakes and roasts rise and brown evenly. In a cold oven, the cooking time changes and so does the result.
  4. Sauce: boil the cream, butter and sugar for 2 minutes.💡 Why it matters: Boiling too hard breaks delicate ingredients and can curdle sauces with cream or egg. A gentle simmer is almost always enough — and safer.
  5. As soon as the cake comes out of the oven, poke it with a fork and slowly pour the hot sauce over it — it drinks it all up.
  6. Serve warm.

Whipped cream or vanilla ice creamCustard — the classic South African pairingCoffee, after a braai
Lili's tipPour the sauce over the piping-hot cake in two goes: half, wait for it to soak in, then the other half. That is what makes it moist inside.

Mashed avocado with lime, onion and cilantro. Ready in 10 minutes and gone in 5.

  1. Cut the avocados open, remove the pits and scoop the flesh into a bowl.
  2. Mash with a fork — chunky, never in a blender.

MexicanMedium ●●○⏱ 35 minServes 4

Fried dough sticks rolled in cinnamon sugar, for dipping in thick, hot chocolate.

👩‍🍳 Method

  1. Boil the water with the butter and salt. Add the flour all at once and stir until it forms a smooth ball (it is the same dough as the rissoles!).💡 Why it matters: Boiling too hard breaks delicate ingredients and can curdle sauces with cream or egg. A gentle simmer is almost always enough — and safer.
  2. Take it off the heat, let it cool a little and add the eggs one at a time, beating well — you get a thick, shiny dough.💡 Why it matters: Cooling before cutting or frosting stops cakes from falling apart and frosting from melting and sliding off. The structure sets outside the oven.
  3. Put the dough in a piping bag fitted with a large star tip.
  4. Pipe 12–15 cm strips straight into the hot oil, cutting them with scissors. Fry until golden.
  5. Drain and roll them immediately in the cinnamon sugar, while still hot.💡 Why it matters: Draining well removes extra water or oil — the stuff that softens crusts, thins sauces and makes salads soggy.
  6. Sauce: heat the milk with the chocolate and cornstarch until thickened. Serve the churros with the chocolate on the side, for dipping.

Lili's tipNo piping bag? Use a freezer bag with one corner cut off. The ridges from the star tip are what give the classic crunch, but the flavor is the same.

JapaneseEasy ●○○⏱ 35 minServes 4

Triangular rice balls with a filling, wrapped in seaweed. Japan's go-to snack.

👩‍🍳 Method

  1. Cook the rice with water only (no seasonings) and let it cool a little, covered.💡 Why it matters: Cooling before cutting or frosting stops cakes from falling apart and frosting from melting and sliding off. The structure sets outside the oven.
  2. Wet your hands in salted water — without this, the rice sticks all to you instead of to the little ball.
  3. Put a handful of rice in your palm, make a little dent, and add a spoonful of filling.
  4. Cover with a little more rice and press it into a triangle shape, turning it between your hands, firmly but without squashing it.
  5. Wrap the base with the strip of nori, like a handle.
  6. Eat it within the next few hours — onigiri doesn't like the fridge (the rice hardens).💡 Why it matters: Cold firms up creams and doughs and makes everything easier to cut and handle — and it's also a safety thing with cream and eggs.

Miso soupGreen teaIn a lunch box, like in Japan
Lili's tipRice that is too hot burns your hands, and cold rice won't shape. Lukewarm is the right point — you work it at body temperature, like with sandwiches.

The Japanese cabbage 'pizza-pancake': crispy on the outside, soft on the inside, with sauces on top.

Little potato pillows that float when they're ready. Easier than they look.

The Italian cream pudding that should wobble when you shake the plate. Only 4 ingredients.

👩‍🍳 Method

  1. Soak the gelatin in cold water for 5 minutes.
  2. Heat the cream with the sugar and vanilla until almost boiling — without letting it boil.💡 Why it matters: Boiling too hard breaks delicate ingredients and can curdle sauces with cream or egg. A gentle simmer is almost always enough — and safer.
  3. Take it off the heat, add the squeezed-out gelatin and stir until completely dissolved.
  4. Pour into small glasses or molds and refrigerate for at least 4 hours.
  5. Serve in the glasses, with fruit on top — unmolding is optional and risky.

Tall, fluffy and golden, stacked with butter and syrup. The breakfast from the movies.

👩‍🍳 Method

  1. Mix the dry ingredients in a large bowl.
  2. Whisk the milk, eggs and butter and pour over the dry ingredients. Stir only until combined — small lumps are good, overmixed batter makes rubbery pancakes.

  1. Oven at 200°C, with the pan or skillet inside heating up — a hot pan makes the crust.💡 Why it matters: A hot oven from minute one makes cakes and roasts rise and brown evenly. In a cold oven, the cooking time changes and so does the result.

  1. Cook the cod for 8 minutes, save the cooking water and shred it, removing the bones and skin.💡 Why it matters: Cooking water holds starch and salt: it helps sauces bind, shine and cling to the food instead of staying watery on the plate.
  2. Sauté the onion and garlic in olive oil until soft and sweet, without browning too much.💡 Why it matters: Browning creates brand-new flavor — it's the reaction that gives color and depth. Wet food or a cold pan steams instead of browning, so dry things well and don't crowd the pan.

  6. Oven at 200°C for 20 minutes, until bubbling and golden on top. Rest 5 minutes before serving.💡 Why it matters: Resting isn't wasted time: juices redistribute and doughs relax. Cutting or unmolding too early loses liquid, air and texture.

PortugueseEasy ●○○⏱ 25 minServes 4

A smooth milk-and-lemon custard with a burnt-sugar crust on top.

👩‍🍳 Method

  1. Heat the milk with the lemon peel and cinnamon until almost boiling. Take it off the heat and let the flavors infuse for 5 minutes.💡 Why it matters: Boiling too hard breaks delicate ingredients and can curdle sauces with cream or egg. A gentle simmer is almost always enough — and safer.
  2. Beat the yolks, sugar and cornstarch until pale.
  3. Pour the hot milk in a thin stream over the yolks, stirring constantly, so they don't cook all of a sudden.
  4. Return everything to low heat and stir until it thickens like a custard. Don't let it boil.💡 Why it matters: Low heat gives sauces time to thicken and flavors time to come together, without burning the bottom or curdling cream and eggs.
  5. Pour into bowls, let it cool and refrigerate for at least 2 hours.💡 Why it matters: Cooling before cutting or frosting stops cakes from falling apart and frosting from melting and sliding off. The structure sets outside the oven.
  6. Before serving, sprinkle with sugar and burn it with a kitchen torch or a hot iron until it forms a crust.

AmericanMedium ●●○⏱ 50 minServes 4

Chicken marinated in buttermilk, well breaded and fried until golden and crackly.

👩‍🍳 Method

  1. Marinate the chicken in the buttermilk with salt for at least 2 hours (overnight is better). The acid tenderizes the meat.💡 Why it matters: Marinating gives salt and spices time to get inside the food — the flavor ends up within, not just on the surface.
  2. Mix the flour with the spices and salt. Add 2 spoonfuls of the marinade to the flour and rub it in — the lumps become extra crust.💡 Why it matters: Marinating gives salt and spices time to get inside the food — the flavor ends up within, not just on the surface.
  3. Coat the chicken in the flour, pressing well so it sticks. Rest 10 minutes: the crust holds on better.💡 Why it matters: Resting isn't wasted time: juices redistribute and doughs relax. Cutting or unmolding too early loses liquid, air and texture.
  4. Heat oil over medium heat (about 170°C) in a deep pot.
  5. Fry for 12 to 15 minutes, turning once, until well golden and cooked through. Drain on a rack, not on paper — paper softens the crust.💡 Why it matters: Draining well removes extra water or oil — the stuff that softens crusts, thins sauces and makes salads soggy.
  6. Salt on top as soon as it comes out of the oil. Rest 5 minutes.💡 Why it matters: Resting isn't wasted time: juices redistribute and doughs relax. Cutting or unmolding too early loses liquid, air and texture.

Golden waffles, crispy on the outside and fluffy on the inside — the weekend breakfast.

👩‍🍳 Method

  1. Mix the dry ingredients. Add the milk, yolks and butter and stir only until combined.
  2. Beat the egg whites to stiff peaks and fold them in gently — the air in the whites is what makes waffles light.💡 Why it matters: Folding gently keeps the air in beaten egg whites and whipped cream — that air is the lightness. Beating hard throws it away.

  5. Serve right away, stacked, with berries and syrup.

South AfricanMedium ●●○⏱ 50 minServes 6

Little spiced dough fritters, fried and soaked in a ginger-and-cinnamon syrup. Sweet, sticky and irresistible.

👩‍🍳 Method

  1. Make the syrup first: boil the sugar, water, ginger and cinnamon for 5 minutes. Let it cool — the syrup must be cold and the fritters hot.💡 Why it matters: Boiling too hard breaks delicate ingredients and can curdle sauces with cream or egg. A gentle simmer is almost always enough — and safer.
  2. Mix the flour, baking powder, spices and salt. Add the egg, a little butter and the warm milk until you have a soft dough.
  3. Knead for 5 minutes, cover and rest for 30 minutes.💡 Why it matters: Resting isn't wasted time: juices redistribute and doughs relax. Cutting or unmolding too early loses liquid, air and texture.
  4. Roll it out to 1 cm thick, cut rectangles, make a slit in the middle and pull one end through it (the classic braided shape, simplified).
  5. Fry in medium oil until well golden.
  6. Drain for a few seconds and dip them right away into the cold syrup. Sprinkle with shredded coconut.💡 Why it matters: Draining well removes extra water or oil — the stuff that softens crusts, thins sauces and makes salads soggy.

Rooibos tea, like in South AfricaCoffeeAs a sharing dessert, on little plates

  1. Cook the chicken in the broth with half an onion and salt, for 20 minutes. Take it out, shred it and save the broth.

🧺 Ingredients

  2. With your fingers, rub the cold butter into the flour until it looks like coarse sand.
  3. Add the oats, the rest of the sugar and cinnamon, and the salt. Don't knead: it should stay in lumps.💡 Why it matters: Resting isn't wasted time: juices redistribute and doughs relax. Cutting or unmolding too early loses liquid, air and texture.
  4. Spread the crust over the fruit without pressing it down.
  5. Oven at 180°C for 30 to 35 minutes, until bubbling at the edges and golden on top.💡 Why it matters: A hot oven from minute one makes cakes and roasts rise and brown evenly. In a cold oven, the cooking time changes and so does the result.
  6. Rest 10 minutes and serve warm.💡 Why it matters: Resting isn't wasted time: juices redistribute and doughs relax. Cutting or unmolding too early loses liquid, air and texture.

A creamy tomato soup with deep, slightly sweet flavor from oven-roasted tomatoes. Simple, cheap, and perfect for using up very ripe tomatoes.

🧺 Ingredients

For 4 people
  • 1 kg ripe tomatoes, halved
  • 1 onion, cut into chunks
  • 4 cloves garlic, unpeeled
  • 3 tbsp olive oil
  • 1 tsp sugar
  • 500 ml vegetable broth
  • 100 ml heavy cream (optional)
  • 1 tsp salt
  • black pepper to taste
  • fresh basil leaves

👩‍🍳 Method

  1. Heat the oven to 200°C (about 400°F). Put the tomatoes, onion and garlic on a baking tray, drizzle with olive oil and season with salt and pepper.
  2. Roast about 30 minutes, until the tomatoes are soft and the edges are browning.💡 Why it matters: Browning creates brand-new flavor — it's the reaction that gives color and depth. Wet food or a cold pan steams instead of browning, so dry things well and don't crowd the pan.
  3. Squeeze the garlic out of its skin and put everything in a pot with the vegetable broth and sugar.
  4. Simmer 5 minutes and blend with an immersion blender until smooth.
  5. Stir in the cream if using, taste and adjust the salt. Serve with basil on top.💡 Why it matters: Tasting at the end is what separates 'almost good' from 'really good': salt, acidity and heat can be fixed in seconds — but only if you taste.

📸 The process, in photos — and why each phase matters

💡 Lili's tip
If your tomatoes are winter ones with little sweetness, the sugar and the roasting work wonders: roasting concentrates the flavor.

A smooth, deeply flavored mushroom soup that tastes like a restaurant's but cooks in one pot. Wonderful on cold days.

🧺 Ingredients

For 4 people
  • 500 g fresh mushrooms, sliced
  • 1 onion, chopped
  • 2 cloves garlic, minced
  • 2 tbsp butter
  • 1 tbsp olive oil
  • 2 tbsp all-purpose flour
  • 700 ml vegetable broth
  • 150 ml heavy cream
  • 1 tsp salt
  • pepper and thyme to taste

👩‍🍳 Method

  1. Heat the butter with the olive oil in a pot and soften the onion for 3 minutes.
  2. Add the mushrooms and garlic and cook 6 to 8 minutes, until the mushrooms brown and release their water.💡 Why it matters: Browning creates brand-new flavor — it's the reaction that gives color and depth. Wet food or a cold pan steams instead of browning, so dry things well and don't crowd the pan.
  3. Sprinkle in the flour, stir 1 minute, then add the broth little by little, stirring all the time.
  4. Bring to a simmer and cook 10 minutes on low heat.💡 Why it matters: Low heat gives sauces time to thicken and flavors time to come together, without burning the bottom or curdling cream and eggs.
  5. Blend half the soup (or all of it, if you like it very smooth), stir in the cream and thyme, and adjust the salt and pepper.💡 Why it matters: Tasting at the end is what separates 'almost good' from 'really good': salt, acidity and heat can be fixed in seconds — but only if you taste.

📸 The process, in photos — and why each phase matters

💡 Lili's tip
Don't crowd the pot when cooking the mushrooms: with space they brown instead of steaming, and the flavor changes completely.

Japan's most famous soup: a light, savory broth with little cubes of tofu and seaweed. Ready in minutes and pure comfort.

🧺 Ingredients

For 2 people
  • 700 ml water
  • 1 tsp dashi powder (or vegetable broth powder)
  • 3 tbsp miso paste
  • 150 g firm tofu, in small cubes
  • 1 tbsp dried wakame seaweed
  • 2 spring onions, thinly sliced
  • 1 tsp soy sauce
  • 1 tsp sesame oil (optional)

👩‍🍳 Method

  1. Soak the seaweed in cold water for 5 minutes, drain and set aside.💡 Why it matters: Draining well removes extra water or oil — the stuff that softens crusts, thins sauces and makes salads soggy.
  2. Heat the water with the dashi until almost boiling, but don't let it fully boil.💡 Why it matters: Boiling too hard breaks delicate ingredients and can curdle sauces with cream or egg. A gentle simmer is almost always enough — and safer.
  3. Lower the heat, add the tofu and seaweed and warm through for 2 minutes.
  4. Take the pot off the heat and dissolve the miso paste in a ladle of hot broth, then stir it into the soup.
  5. Add the soy sauce and sesame oil, sprinkle the spring onions and serve right away.

📸 The process, in photos — and why each phase matters

💡 Lili's tip
Miso should never boil: strong heat ruins its flavor and aroma. Always dissolve it at the end, off the heat.

The spicy Roman classic: penne in a tomato sauce with garlic and chili. Few ingredients, lots of character — and ready in no time.

👩‍🍳 Method

  1. Cook the penne in well-salted water until al dente. Save a cup of the cooking water.💡 Why it matters: Cooking water holds starch and salt: it helps sauces bind, shine and cling to the food instead of staying watery on the plate.
  2. Heat the olive oil in a large skillet and cook the garlic and chili for 1 minute, without burning.
  3. Add the tomatoes, salt and sugar, crush with a spoon and cook 12 minutes until the sauce thickens a little.
  4. Move the penne into the skillet with some cooking water and toss for 1 to 2 minutes.💡 Why it matters: Cooking water holds starch and salt: it helps sauces bind, shine and cling to the food instead of staying watery on the plate.
  5. Serve with chopped parsley and parmesan, if you like.

One of Portugal's most loved oven dishes: cod loins under a golden crust of cornbread, garlic and olive oil. A guaranteed celebration dish.

Soften the onion with the bay leaf and half the olive oil, without browning much.💡 Why it matters: Browning creates brand-new flavor — it's the reaction that gives color and depth. A thick, hearty beef and bean chili with warm spices and a rich sauce. Big-pot food, perfect for sharing.

🧺 Ingredients

For 6 people
  • 600 g ground beef
  • 1 large onion, chopped
  • 3 cloves garlic, minced

VegetarianEasy ●○○⏱ 30 minServes 4

🧺 Ingredients

For 4 people
  • 4 large flour tortillas
  • 1 can cooked black beans (400 g), drained
  • 200 g cooked white rice
  • 1 small onion, finely chopped
  • 2 cloves garlic, minced
  • 1 tsp ground cumin
  • 1 tsp smoked paprika
  • 150 g shredded cheese
  • 1 red bell pepper, thinly sliced
  • 4 tbsp sour cream or Greek yogurt
  • salt and pepper
  • 1 tbsp olive oil
Your rating:
Prep15 min
Cook15 min
Total30 min
DifficultyEasy ●○○
Serves4
Calories~540 kcal
Protein21 g
Fat24 g
Carbs59 g

Estimated nutrition per serving, calculated from the ingredients.

Warm tortillas filled with seasoned beans, rice and melted cheese. A simple, cheap meal that really fills you up.

👩‍🍳 Method

  1. Heat the olive oil in a large skillet and cook the onion and bell pepper for 4 to 5 minutes, until soft.
  2. Add the garlic, cumin and paprika, stir for 1 minute, then add the drained beans.💡 Why it matters: Draining well removes extra water or oil — the stuff that softens crusts, thins sauces and makes salads soggy.
  3. Mash some of the beans with the back of the spoon, season with salt and pepper, and cook for 5 minutes, until creamy.
  4. Stir the cooked rice into the beans and taste for salt.💡 Why it matters: Tasting at the end is what separates 'almost good' from 'really good': salt, acidity and heat can be fixed in seconds — but only if you taste.
  5. Warm the tortillas in a dry skillet, 30 seconds per side, so they bend without breaking.
  6. Fill each tortilla with the mixture, the cheese and a spoonful of sour cream, roll it up tightly folding in the sides, and toast for 1 to 2 minutes in the hot skillet, seam side down.💡 Why it matters: Folding gently keeps the air in beaten egg whites and whipped cream — that air is the lightness. Beating hard throws it away.

Green salad with tomato and cornGuacamole or spicy tomato salsaOven potato wedges
Lili's tipIf the beans get dry, add 2 to 3 tablespoons of hot water — they turn creamy again.

Chicken Korma

Frango korma

Estimated nutrition per serving, calculated from the ingredients.

A mild, creamy Indian curry with tender chicken in a yogurt, coconut and almond sauce. All the perfume of the spices, without real heat.

🧺 Ingredients

For 4 people
  • 600 g chicken breast or thighs, cubed
  • 150 g plain yogurt
  • 2 tbsp vegetable oil or ghee
  • 1 large onion, finely chopped
  • 3 cloves garlic, minced
  • 1 tbsp grated fresh ginger
  • 2 tsp garam masala
  • 1 tsp ground coriander
  • 1 tsp turmeric
  • 200 ml coconut milk
  • 50 g ground almonds
  • salt

👩‍🍳 Method

  1. Mix the chicken with half the yogurt, 1 teaspoon of the garam masala and a pinch of salt. Let it marinate for 15 minutes (or longer, if you have time).💡 Why it matters: Marinating gives salt and spices time to get inside the food — the flavor ends up within, not just on the surface.
  2. Heat the oil in a pot and cook the onion over medium heat for 8 to 10 minutes, until deeply golden.
  3. Add the garlic and ginger, stir for 1 minute, then add the remaining spices with 2 tablespoons of water. Stir for 1 more minute.
  4. Add the chicken with its marinade and cook for 5 to 6 minutes, stirring, until it loses its raw color.💡 Why it matters: Marinating gives salt and spices time to get inside the food — the flavor ends up within, not just on the surface.
  5. Lower the heat, add the coconut milk, the ground almonds and the rest of the yogurt, spoon by spoon, stirring all the time so it does not curdle.💡 Why it matters: Resting isn't wasted time: juices redistribute and doughs relax. Cutting or unmolding too early loses liquid, air and texture.
  6. Simmer gently for 10 to 12 minutes, until the chicken is tender and the sauce is creamy. Taste for salt and serve with fresh cilantro on top, if you have it.💡 Why it matters: Tasting at the end is what separates 'almost good' from 'really good': salt, acidity and heat can be fixed in seconds — but only if you taste.

📸 The process, in photos — and why each phase matters

💡 Lili's tip
Yogurt curdles over high heat: always lower the heat and add it a little at a time, stirring nonstop.
🍽️ What to serve with it
Basmati rice or jeera rice · Warm naan bread · Cucumber and yogurt salad

Aloo Gobi (Potato and Cauliflower)

Aloo gobi (batata e couve-flor)
VegetarianEasy ●○○⏱ 40 minServes 4

🧺 Ingredients

For 4 people
  • 400 g potatoes, in medium cubes
  • 400 g cauliflower, in florets
  • 1 onion, chopped
  • 2 ripe tomatoes, diced
  • 1 tbsp grated fresh ginger
  • 2 cloves garlic, minced
  • 1 tsp cumin seeds
  • 1 tsp turmeric
  • 1 tsp ground coriander

  • salt and fresh cilantro

India's classic vegetarian dish: potato and cauliflower wrapped in golden spices. Simple, cheap and full of flavor.

👩‍🍳 Method

  1. Heat the oil in a wide pot and add the cumin seeds; when they start to pop, add the onion and cook for 5 minutes.
  2. Add the garlic and ginger, stir for 1 minute, then add the tomato with the turmeric, ground coriander and salt.
  3. Cook the tomato for 4 to 5 minutes, stirring, until it becomes a thick paste and the oil starts to separate at the edges.
  4. Add the potatoes and cauliflower, mix well in the paste, cover and cook over low heat for 15 to 18 minutes, stirring now and then.💡 Why it matters: Low heat gives sauces time to thicken and flavors time to come together, without burning the bottom or curdling cream and eggs.
  5. If it gets too dry, sprinkle in 2 to 3 tablespoons of hot water — aloo gobi is a dry curry, without much sauce.
  6. When the potato is tender, add the garam masala, let it rest covered for 5 minutes and serve with fresh cilantro.💡 Why it matters: Resting isn't wasted time: juices redistribute and doughs relax. Cutting or unmolding too early loses liquid, air and texture.

Lili's tipCut the potato and cauliflower into pieces of the same size: they finish cooking together and nothing stays raw or falls apart.

Chocolate Mousse

Mousse de chocolate
Prep · 20 min|Cook · 5 min|Serves · 4|~520 kcal
Your rating:

A light, intense mousse made with dark chocolate, cream and whipped egg whites. An elegant dessert with no oven needed.

🧺 Ingredients

For 4 people
  • 200 g dark chocolate (70%), chopped
  • 1 tbsp butter
  • 3 eggs, yolks and whites separated
  • 200 ml heavy cream, very cold
  • 2 tbsp sugar
  • 1 tsp vanilla extract
  • a pinch of salt
  • chocolate shavings or cocoa, to serve
  • 100 g fresh berries, to serve

👩‍🍳 Method

  1. Melt the chocolate with the butter in a bowl over hot water (or in the microwave, in short bursts), stirring until smooth. Let it cool for 5 minutes.💡 Why it matters: Cooling before cutting or frosting stops cakes from falling apart and frosting from melting and sliding off. The structure sets outside the oven.
  2. Mix the yolks, one at a time, into the warm chocolate, then add the vanilla and the pinch of salt.
  3. Whip the cold cream until it holds firm but still soft peaks.
  4. In another bowl, beat the egg whites with the sugar until glossy and stiff.
  5. Fold the cream into the chocolate first, then the egg whites, in two additions, with gentle upward movements so you do not lose the air.💡 Why it matters: Folding gently keeps the air in beaten egg whites and whipped cream — that air is the lightness. Beating hard throws it away.
  6. Divide among small cups and chill for at least 2 hours. Serve with chocolate shavings or berries.💡 Why it matters: Cold firms up creams and doughs and makes everything easier to cut and handle — and it's also a safety thing with cream and eggs.

Total25 min
DifficultyEasy ●○○

Carbs36 g

Panna Cotta with Berries

Panna cotta com frutos vermelhos
Prep · 10 min|Cook · 5 min|Serves · 4|~430 kcal
Your rating:

Italy's simplest dessert: soft vanilla cream crowned with berries. It takes minutes to make and always impresses.

🧺 Ingredients

For 4 people
  • 400 ml heavy cream
  • 100 ml milk
  • 60 g sugar
  • 2 sheets gelatin
  • 1 tsp vanilla extract
  • 200 g mixed berries (strawberries, raspberries, blueberries)
  • 1 tbsp sugar (for the berries)
  • 1 tsp lemon juice

👩‍🍳 Method

  1. Soak the gelatin sheets in cold water for 5 to 10 minutes, until soft.
  2. Heat the cream with the milk, sugar and vanilla until it starts to steam — without letting it boil.💡 Why it matters: Boiling too hard breaks delicate ingredients and can curdle sauces with cream or egg. A gentle simmer is almost always enough — and safer.
  3. Take it off the heat, squeeze the gelatin well and dissolve it in the hot cream, stirring until it disappears.
  4. Strain, divide among 4 small cups or molds and chill for at least 4 hours.💡 Why it matters: Cold firms up creams and doughs and makes everything easier to cut and handle — and it's also a safety thing with cream and eggs.
  5. Crush half the berries with the sugar and lemon juice into a rustic sauce; stir in the rest of the berries whole.💡 Why it matters: Resting isn't wasted time: juices redistribute and doughs relax. Cutting or unmolding too early loses liquid, air and texture.
  6. Serve the panna cotta very cold with the berry sauce on top.

Apple Cinnamon Cake

Bolo de maçã e canela
Prep · 20 min|Cook · 40 min|Serves · 8|~365 kcal
Your rating:

A soft, moist cake full of little apple pieces, with that cinnamon smell that fills the house. Perfect for an afternoon snack.

🧺 Ingredients

For 8 people
  • 3 apples, peeled and diced small
  • 3 eggs
  • 180 g sugar
  • 100 ml vegetable oil
  • 250 g all-purpose flour
  • 1 tbsp baking powder
  • 2 tsp ground cinnamon
  • 1 tsp vanilla extract
  • a pinch of salt
  • sugar and cinnamon, for dusting

👩‍🍳 Method

  1. Heat the oven to 180°C (350°F). Grease and flour a round cake pan, 22 to 24 cm (9 to 10 in).
  2. Beat the eggs with the sugar until pale and creamy. Add the oil and vanilla and mix well.
  3. Sift in the flour with the baking powder, cinnamon and salt, and fold into the batter without overmixing.💡 Why it matters: Sifting removes lumps and adds air to dry ingredients — lighter batters and sauces without little balls.
  4. Fold the apple pieces into the batter — it looks like a lot of apple, but that is what keeps the cake moist.💡 Why it matters: Folding gently keeps the air in beaten egg whites and whipped cream — that air is the lightness. Beating hard throws it away.
  5. Pour into the pan, smooth the top and dust with a little sugar and cinnamon.
  6. Bake for 35 to 40 minutes, until golden and a toothpick comes out clean. Let it cool for 10 minutes before unmolding.💡 Why it matters: Cooling before cutting or frosting stops cakes from falling apart and frosting from melting and sliding off. The structure sets outside the oven.

  5. Scoop balls with a tablespoon of dough, place them on the sheets with space between them and flatten them slightly.

For 4 people

Brazilian Cornmeal Cake (Bolo de Fubá)

Bolo de fubá
Prep · 10 min|Cook · 40 min|Serves · 8|~450 kcal
Your rating:

Brazil's afternoon-coffee cake: fine cornmeal, a soft crumb and pure grandma's-kitchen smell. A simple blender cake.

🧺 Ingredients

For 8 people
  • 3 eggs
  • 1,5 cup sugar
  • 0,5 cup oil
  • 1 cup milk
  • 1,5 cup fine cornmeal (fubá)
  • 1 cup all-purpose flour
  • 1 tbsp baking powder
  • 1 pinch salt
  • 1 tsp fennel seeds (optional)

👩‍🍳 Method

  1. Heat the oven to 180°C / 350°F and grease a tube pan (or a 9-in round pan) with butter and a dusting of cornmeal.

  3. Add the cornmeal, flour and salt and blend just until combined — don't overmix.
  4. Add the baking powder (and fennel, if using) and pulse two or three times.
  5. Pour into the pan and bake 35–40 minutes, until golden and a toothpick comes out clean.
  6. Cool 10 minutes before unmolding; serve warm or at room temperature.💡 Why it matters: Cooling before cutting or frosting stops cakes from falling apart and frosting from melting and sliding off. The structure sets outside the oven.

Três bruschettas diferentes no mesmo prato: tomate com manjericão, pesto e ricotta com mel. Um trio para agradar a toda a gente.

👩‍🍳 Method

  1. Corta o tomate em cubinhos, junta sal, um fio de azeite e o manjericão picado. Deixa repousar 10 minutos.
  2. Mistura a ricotta com uma pitada de sal e pimenta até ficar cremosa.
  3. Torra as fatias de pão dos dois lados até ficarem crocantes.
  4. Esfrega o dente de alho cortado em cada fatia ainda quente.
  5. Monta o trio: umas fatias com tomate, outras com pesto, outras com ricotta e um fio de mel.
  6. Termina com um fio de azeite e folhas de manjericão e serve logo.

As panquecas mais fofas de sempre: a ricotta e as claras batidas fazem-nas crescer como nuvens. Com frutos vermelhos e mel, é o brunch perfeito.

🧺 Ingredients

For 4 people
  • 250 g ricotta
  • 3 egg (yolks and whites separated)

👩‍🍳 Method

  3. Bate as claras em castelo e envolve-as na massa com cuidado, em duas vezes.
  4. Aquece uma frigideira com um pouco de manteiga e cozinha colheradas de massa 2 minutos de cada lado, até dourarem.

Chá preto bem gelado com xarope de pêssego caseiro. Sabe a verão em jarro e desaparece num instante.

👩‍🍳 Method

  1. Corta dois pêssegos em fatias e ferve-os com o açúcar e 250 ml da água durante 5 minutos, esmagando de leve.
  2. Tira do lume, deixa o xarope infundir 15 minutos e coa.

  5. Serve num jarro com muito gelo, rodelas do terceiro pêssego e folhas de hortelã.

Seasonings & Spices

know your seasonings

Seasonings are the soul of cooking: they turn the same ingredients into dishes from different countries. Here are the names, the photos and what each one is for.

Coarse salt
Sal grosso
Enhances every flavor; perfect for grilled meats and roasts.
Black pepper
Pimenta preta
Adds warmth and aroma; great on almost everything, freshly ground.
Paprika
Colorau / páprica
Adds color and gentle sweetness to meats, potatoes and sauces.
Smoked paprika
Páprica fumada
Smoky flavor for meats, potatoes and sauces; a little goes far.
Turmeric
Açafrão-da-terra / curcuma
Golden color and earthy flavor for rice, soups and curries.
Curry powder
Caril em pó
Warm all-in-one blend for chicken, vegetable and prawn curries.
Garam masala
Garam masala
Aromatic Indian blend; add at the end to curries and lentils.
Cumin
Cominhos
Warm, earthy flavor; great in curries, beans and rice.
Coriander seeds
Sementes de coentros
Ground, they add a citrusy note to curries, soups and marinades.
Cinnamon
Canela
Sweet and warm; perfect in desserts, cakes and some curries.
Nutmeg
Noz-moscada
A little grated goes far in béchamel, mash and cakes.
Cloves
Cravinho
Strong, warm aroma; use just a few in rice, meats and sweets.
Cardamom
Cardamomo
Intense perfume for coffee, tea, rice and desserts.
Ginger
Gengibre
Fresh and zesty; great in teas, soups, curries and stir-fries.
Chili (piri-piri)
Piripíri / malagueta
The house heat; use sparingly in sauces and grilled dishes.
Bay leaves
Louro
Aromatic leaves for soups, stews and rice; remove before serving.
Oregano
Orégãos
A classic on pizzas, pasta, tomato sauces and salads.
Basil
Manjericão
Fresh and sweet; add at the end to pasta, tomato and salads.
Thyme
Tomilho
Delicate herb for roast meats, soups and oven vegetables.
Rosemary
Alecrim
Strong piney aroma; perfect with potatoes, chicken and lamb.
Parsley
Salsa
Freshness and color to finish any dish; use it raw.
Garlic
Alho
The base of almost everything; sizzle first to build flavor.
Fennel seeds
Erva-doce / funcho
Sweet, light seeds; lovely with fish, bread and teas.
Sesame seeds
Sésamo
Toasted, it adds crunch and nutty flavor to salads and noodles.

The Guide

Gain or Lose Weight

eat well, with a simple plan

No magic: losing weight means using a little more than you eat; gaining means eating a little more than you use — with real food. These recommendations use the estimated nutrition values of each recipe in this book.

🥗 To lose weight

  • Fill half your plate with vegetables and salad — a full plate without the calories.
  • Protein at every meal (fish, chicken, eggs, beans and lentils): it keeps you full for longer.
  • Start with soup: it helps you eat less of the main dish.
  • Measure the oil (about 1 tbsp per meal) and grill or roast instead of frying.
  • Drink water through the day; often "hunger" is really thirst. Skip sodas and sugary juices.
  • Eat without screens and sleep well — distracted eating makes you go back for more without noticing.

The lightest recipes in this book

💪 To gain weight (and muscle)

  • Eat a little more at every meal and add 2–3 snacks a day — this book's smoothies and shakes are perfect for that.
  • Protein at every meal: meat, fish, eggs, milk, beans and lentils give muscles the material to grow.
  • Add good extras to your dishes: olive oil, peanut butter, avocado, cheese and nuts.
  • Don't skip meals: your body can only build with extra material, every day.
  • Strength-train 2–4 times a week — that's the training that turns food into muscle.
  • Be patient: gaining ½–1 lb (250–500 g) a week is a good, sustainable pace.

🍽️ The plate method

Half the plate: vegetables and salad. One quarter: protein (meat, fish, eggs, beans). One quarter: carbs (rice, pasta, potatoes, bread). To lose, shrink the carbs and the oil a little; to gain, add more carbs plus a good fat.

An honest note: the nutrition values in this book are estimates calculated from the ingredients, and these pages are general kitchen guidance — they don't replace advice from a doctor or a registered dietitian.

¼ whole grains

The Guide

What Nutrition Means

read the numbers without fear

Every recipe in this book shows four numbers per serving: calories, protein, fat and carbs. This page explains, in simple words, what each one is, what it does in your body and why it matters.

🔥 Calories (kcal)

A calorie measures the energy in food. Your body spends that energy on everything: breathing, thinking, walking, training. Eat more energy than you use and your body stores the extra — weight goes up; eat less and it uses the reserves — weight goes down. On average, an adult needs about 2,000 kcal a day, but it varies with size, age and activity.

Why it matters: it's the number that, across the whole day, decides whether you gain or lose weight.

🥩 Protein

Your body's building material: muscles, skin, hair, nails and immune defenses. It's also the nutrient that keeps you full the longest. Sources: meat, fish, eggs, milk and cheese, beans, lentils and chickpeas. A simple reference: about 1 g per kilo (roughly 0.5 g per pound) of body weight a day for most people — and more (1.4–2 g per kilo) if you strength-train or want to gain muscle.

Why it matters: without enough protein, you lose muscle instead of fat — or build no muscle at all.

🍞 Carbs (carbohydrates)

Your body and brain's quick fuel: they turn into energy for the day and for training. Sources: rice, pasta, bread, potatoes, oats and fruit. Whole-grain ones, and ones that come with fiber, are used more slowly and keep you full for longer.

Why it matters: carbs aren't "bad" — they're the battery. The right amount depends on your goal and how much you move.

🥑 Fat

Fat stores energy, protects your organs and is needed to absorb vitamins A, D, E and K and to make hormones. Not all fat is equal: olive oil, avocado, nuts and oily fish bring the "good" fats; lots of frying and processed-meat fat, in excess, weighs on heart health.

Why it matters: too little fat is harmful — quality and quantity make the difference.

🌾 Fiber

The part of plants your body doesn't digest — and that's why it helps: it feeds your gut, slows down blood-sugar rises and fills your stomach. Sources: vegetables, fruit with the skin on, beans, lentils, oats and whole-grain bread. The common reference is about 25–30 g a day.

Why it matters: a happy gut, controlled hunger and steadier blood sugar.

🧂 Salt and sugar — the hidden ones

They don't appear in this book's numbers, but they're worth knowing: extra sugar becomes stored energy and hunger spikes; extra salt makes you retain water and, over time, weighs on blood pressure. Read packaged-food labels — that's often where they hide.

📏 "Per serving" — and how to use these numbers

All values in this book are per serving (the recipe divided by the number of people it serves) and are estimates calculated from the ingredients: they're for comparing recipes and planning your day, not lab values. To lose weight, pick the lower-calorie, good-protein recipes more often; to gain, pick the higher-calorie, high-protein ones. And remember: no single number makes a recipe "good" or "bad" — what counts is the whole day and week.
